passages.text: “Run for cover, O sons of Benjamin; flee from Jerusalem! Sound the ram’s horn in Tekoa; send up a signal over Beth-haccherem, for disaster looms from the north, even great destruction.
passages.sermon:
The sons of Benjamin must run for cover.
They must flee from Jerusalem.
People in Tekoa must sound the ram’s horn.
People in Beth-haccherem must send up a signal.
Disaster is coming from the north.
Great destruction is approaching.
passages.original: הָעִ֣זוּ׀ בְּנֵ֣י בִניָמִ֗ן מִקֶּ֙רֶב֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וּבִתְק֙וֹעַ֙ תִּקְע֣וּ שׁוֹפָ֔ר וְעַל־ בֵּ֥ית הַכֶּ֖רֶם שְׂא֣וּ מַשְׂאֵ֑ת כִּ֥י רָעָ֛ה נִשְׁקְפָ֥ה מִצָּפ֖וֹן וְשֶׁ֥בֶר גָּדֽוֹל׃

passages.text: Though she is beautiful and delicate, I will destroy the Daughter of Zion.
passages.sermon: The Daughter of Zion is beautiful.\r\nThe Daughter of Zion is delicate.\r\nI will destroy the Daughter of Zion.
passages.original: הַנָּוָה֙ וְהַמְּעֻנָּגָ֔ה דָּמִ֖יתִי בַּת־ צִיּֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Shepherds and their flocks will come against her; they will pitch their tents all around her, each tending his own portion: ‘Prepare for battle against her; rise up, let us attack at noon. Woe to us, for the daylight is fading; the evening shadows grow long.
passages.sermon:
Shepherds will come against the Daughter of Zion.
They will bring their flocks with them.
They will set up their tents all around her.
Each shepherd will graze his flock in his own place.
They will say, “Prepare for battle against her.”
They will say, “Rise up. Let us attack at noon.”
They will say, “Woe to us, for the day is fading.”
They will say, “The evening shadows are growing long.”
passages.original: אֵלֶ֛יהָ יָבֹ֥אוּ רֹעִ֖ים וְעֶדְרֵיהֶ֑ם תָּקְע֨וּ עָלֶ֤יהָ אֹהָלִים֙ סָבִ֔יב רָע֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ אֶת־ יָדֽוֹ׃ קַדְּשׁ֤וּ עָלֶ֙יהָ֙ מִלְחָמָ֔ה ק֖וּמוּ וְנַעֲלֶ֣ה בַֽצָּהֳרָ֑יִם א֥וֹי לָ֙נוּ֙ כִּי־ פָנָ֣ה הַיּ֔וֹם כִּ֥י יִנָּט֖וּ צִלְלֵי־ עָֽרֶב׃

passages.text: Rise up, let us attack by night and destroy her fortresses!’ ”
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks about Jerusalem.
He commands the enemies of Jerusalem.
He says, "Rise up."
He says, "Let us attack by night."
He says, "Let us destroy her fortresses."
passages.original: ק֚וּמוּ וְנַעֲלֶ֣ה בַלָּ֔יְלָה וְנַשְׁחִ֖יתָה אַרְמְנוֹתֶֽיהָ׃ס

passages.text: For this is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Cut down the trees and raise a siege ramp against Jerusalem. This city must be punished; there is nothing but oppression in her midst.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
He commands action.
Cut down the trees.
Build a siege ramp against Jerusalem.
Jerusalem is the city under judgment.
God must punish this city.
Oppression fills Jerusalem.
There is nothing but oppression in her midst.
passages.original: כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת כִּרְת֣וּ עֵצָ֔ה וְשִׁפְכ֥וּ עַל־ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם סֹלְלָ֑ה הִ֚יא הָעִ֣יר הָפְקַ֔ד כֻּלָּ֖הּ עֹ֥שֶׁק בְּקִרְבָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: As a well gushes its water, so she pours out her evil. Violence and destruction resound in her; sickness and wounds are ever before Me.
passages.sermon:
Jerusalem is a city.
Jerusalem pours out evil.
She pours out evil like a well pours out water.
Violence fills Jerusalem.
Destruction fills Jerusalem.
I, the LORD, always see sickness in Jerusalem.
I always see wounds in Jerusalem.
passages.original: כְּהָקִ֥יר בְּוֵר מֵימֶ֔יהָ כֵּ֖ן הֵקֵ֣רָה רָעָתָ֑הּ חָמָ֣ס וָ֠שֹׁד יִשָּׁ֨מַע בָּ֧הּ עַל־ פָּנַ֛י תָּמִ֖יד חֳלִ֥י וּמַכָּֽה׃

passages.text: Be forewarned, O Jerusalem, or I will turn away from you; I will make you a desolation, a land without inhabitant.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks to Jerusalem.
Jerusalem, listen to this warning.
Change your ways now.
If you do not listen, I will turn away from you.
If you do not change, I will make you empty and ruined.
No one will live in your land.
Your city will become a desolation.
passages.original: הִוָּסְרִי֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם פֶּן־ תֵּקַ֥ע נַפְשִׁ֖י מִמֵּ֑ךְ פֶּן־ אֲשִׂימֵ֣ךְ שְׁמָמָ֔ה אֶ֖רֶץ ל֥וֹא נוֹשָֽׁבָה׃פ

passages.text: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Glean the remnant of Israel as thoroughly as a vine. Pass your hand once more like a grape gatherer over the branches.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
The LORD of Hosts commands with authority.
He says, “Glean the remnant of Israel.
Glean them as thoroughly as a vine.
Pass your hand over the branches again.
Do this like a grape gatherer who searches for every grape.”
passages.original: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהֹוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת עוֹלֵ֛ל יְעוֹלְל֥וּ כַגֶּ֖פֶן שְׁאֵרִ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל הָשֵׁב֙ יָדְךָ֔ כְּבוֹצֵ֖ר עַל־ סַלְסִלּֽוֹת׃

passages.text: To whom can I give this warning? Who will listen to me? Look, their ears are closed, so they cannot hear. See, the word of the LORD has become offensive to them; they find no pleasure in it.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Jerusalem.
God wants to warn them.
God asks, “Who will listen to me?”
The people do not listen.
Their ears are closed.
They cannot hear God’s message.
The word of the LORD offends them.
They do not want God’s word.
They find no joy in it.
passages.original: עַל־ מִ֨י אֲדַבְּרָ֤ה וְאָעִ֙ידָה֙ וְיִשְׁמָ֔עוּ הִנֵּה֙ עֲרֵלָ֣ה אָזְנָ֔ם וְלֹ֥א יוּכְל֖וּ לְהַקְשִׁ֑יב הִנֵּ֣ה דְבַר־ יְהוָ֗ה הָיָ֥ה לָהֶ֛ם לְחֶרְפָּ֖ה לֹ֥א יַחְפְּצוּ־ בֽוֹ׃

passages.text: But I am full of the LORD’s wrath; I am tired of holding it back. “Pour it out on the children in the street, and on the young men gathered together. For both husband and wife will be captured, the old and the very old alike.
passages.sermon:
The prophet Jeremiah speaks for the LORD of Hosts.
Jeremiah says he is full of the LORD’s wrath.
He is tired of holding back this anger.
The LORD commands to pour out His wrath on the children in the street.
The LORD commands to pour out His wrath on the young men gathered together.
Husband and wife will both be captured.
The old will be captured.
The very old will also be captured.
passages.original: וְאֵת֩ חֲמַ֨ת יְהוָ֤ה׀ מָלֵ֙אתִי֙ נִלְאֵ֣יתִי הָכִ֔יל שְׁפֹ֤ךְ עַל־ עוֹלָל֙ בַּח֔וּץ וְעַ֛ל ס֥וֹד בַּחוּרִ֖ים יַחְדָּ֑ו כִּֽי־ גַם־ אִ֤ישׁ עִם־ אִשָּׁה֙ יִלָּכֵ֔דוּ זָקֵ֖ן עִם־ מְלֵ֥א יָמִֽים׃

passages.text: Their houses will be turned over to others, their fields and wives as well, for I will stretch out My hand against the inhabitants of the land,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to the people who live in the land.
The LORD says He will act against them.
The LORD will stretch out His hand against the inhabitants of the land.
Other people will take their houses.
Other people will take their fields.
Other people will take their wives.
The LORD Himself declares this.
passages.original: וְנָסַ֤בּוּ בָֽתֵּיהֶם֙ לַאֲחֵרִ֔ים שָׂד֥וֹת וְנָשִׁ֖ים יַחְדָּ֑ו כִּֽי־ אַטֶּ֧ה אֶת־ יָדִ֛י עַל־ יֹשְׁבֵ֥י הָאָ֖רֶץ נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: “For from the least of them to the greatest, all are greedy for gain; from prophet to priest, all practice deceit.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about the people of the land.
He says every person is guilty.
The smallest person is greedy for gain.
The greatest person is greedy for gain.
Every prophet acts dishonestly.
Every priest acts dishonestly.
All seek their own advantage.
All practice deceit.
passages.original: כִּ֤י מִקְּטַנָּם֙ וְעַד־ גְּדוֹלָ֔ם כֻּלּ֖וֹ בּוֹצֵ֣עַ בָּ֑צַע וּמִנָּבִיא֙ וְעַד־ כֹּהֵ֔ן כֻּלּ֖וֹ עֹ֥שֶׂה שָּֽׁקֶר׃

passages.text: They dress the wound of My people with very little care, saying, ‘Peace, peace,’ when there is no peace at all.
passages.sermon:
The leaders and spiritual guides of Israel act carelessly.
They see that My people are wounded.
They try to heal the wound quickly and lightly.
They do not give real help.
They say, “Peace, peace.”
They claim that everything is well.
But there is no peace at all.
passages.original: וַֽיְרַפְּא֞וּ אֶת־ שֶׁ֤בֶר עַמִּי֙ עַל־ נְקַלָּ֔ה לֵאמֹ֖ר שָׁל֣וֹם׀ שָׁל֑וֹם וְאֵ֖ין שָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: Are they ashamed of the abomination they have committed? No, they have no shame at all; they do not even know how to blush. So they will fall among the fallen; when I punish them, they will collapse,” says the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks about the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
They have committed abominations.
They are not ashamed of what they have done.
They do not feel any shame at all.
They do not even know how to blush.
Therefore, they will fall with those who have already fallen.
When I, the LORD, punish them, they will stumble and collapse.
passages.original: הֹבִ֕ישׁוּ כִּ֥י תוֹעֵבָ֖ה עָשׂ֑וּ גַּם־ בּ֣וֹשׁ לֹֽא־ יֵב֗וֹשׁוּ גַּם־ הַכְלִים֙ לֹ֣א יָדָ֔עוּ לָכֵ֞ן יִפְּל֧וּ בַנֹּפְלִ֛ים בְּעֵת־ פְּקַדְתִּ֥ים יִכָּשְׁל֖וּ אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: This is what the LORD says: “Stand at the crossroads and look. Ask for the ancient paths: ‘Where is the good way?’ Then walk in it, and you will find rest for your souls. But they said, ‘We will not walk in it!’
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to the people of Israel.
He gives them a command.
He says, "Stand at the crossroads."
He tells them to look carefully.
He tells them to ask about the ancient paths.
He says, "Ask, 'Where is the good way?'
He commands them to walk in that good way.
He promises, "You will find rest for your souls if you do this."
But the people answer the LORD.
They say, "We will not walk in it."
passages.original: כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֡ה עִמְדוּ֩ עַל־ דְּרָכִ֨ים וּרְא֜וּ וְשַׁאֲל֣וּ׀ לִנְתִב֣וֹת עוֹלָ֗ם אֵי־ זֶ֨ה דֶ֤רֶךְ הַטּוֹב֙ וּלְכוּ־ בָ֔הּ וּמִצְא֥וּ מַרְגּ֖וֹעַ לְנַפְשְׁכֶ֑ם וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ לֹ֥א נֵלֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: I appointed watchmen over you and said, ‘Listen for the sound of the ram’s horn.’ But they answered, ‘We will not listen!’
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
The LORD appointed watchmen over them.
The LORD told the people, "Listen for the sound of the ram’s horn."
The people answered the LORD.
They said, "We will not listen."
passages.original: וַהֲקִמֹתִ֤י עֲלֵיכֶם֙ צֹפִ֔ים הַקְשִׁ֖יבוּ לְק֣וֹל שׁוֹפָ֑ר וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ לֹ֥א נַקְשִֽׁיב׃

passages.text: Therefore hear, O nations, and learn, O congregations, what will happen to them.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to all nations.
He commands the nations to listen.
He calls the congregations to pay attention.
He tells them to learn what will happen to His people.
He wants everyone to understand the consequences for His people.
passages.original: לָכֵ֖ן שִׁמְע֣וּ הַגּוֹיִ֑ם וּדְעִ֥י עֵדָ֖ה אֶת־ אֲשֶׁר־ בָּֽם׃

passages.text: Hear, O earth! I am bringing disaster on this people, the fruit of their own schemes, because they have paid no attention to My word and have rejected My instruction.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to all the earth.
God says, “Listen, earth.
I am bringing disaster on these people.
This disaster comes from their own plans.
They did not listen to My word.
They rejected My instruction.”
passages.original: שִׁמְעִ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י מֵבִ֥יא רָעָ֛ה אֶל־ הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה פְּרִ֣י מַחְשְׁבוֹתָ֑ם כִּ֤י עַל־ דְּבָרַי֙ לֹ֣א הִקְשִׁ֔יבוּ וְתוֹרָתִ֖י וַיִּמְאֲסוּ־ בָֽהּ׃

passages.text: What use to Me is frankincense from Sheba or sweet cane from a distant land? Your burnt offerings are not acceptable; your sacrifices do not please Me.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God asks about their offerings.
God says, “Why do you bring Me frankincense from Sheba?
Why do you bring sweet cane from a distant land?
Your burnt offerings do not please Me.
Your sacrifices are not acceptable to Me.”
passages.original: לָמָּה־ זֶּ֨ה לִ֤י לְבוֹנָה֙ מִשְּׁבָ֣א תָב֔וֹא וְקָנֶ֥ה הַטּ֖וֹב מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מֶרְחָ֑ק עֹלֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ לֹ֣א לְרָצ֔וֹן וְזִבְחֵיכֶ֖ם לֹא־ עָ֥רְבוּ לִֽי׃ס

passages.text: Therefore this is what the LORD says: “I will lay stumbling blocks before this people; fathers and sons alike will be staggered; friends and neighbors will perish.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to the people of Judah.
He says, “I will put obstacles in front of this people.
Fathers will stumble over them.
Sons will stumble too.
They will fall together.
Neighbors will fall.
Friends will fall.
They will all perish.”
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנְנִ֥י נֹתֵ֛ן אֶל־ הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה מִכְשֹׁלִ֑ים וְכָ֣שְׁלוּ בָ֠ם אָב֨וֹת וּבָנִ֥ים יַחְדָּ֛ו שָׁכֵ֥ן וְרֵע֖וֹ יֹאבֵדוּ׃פ

passages.text: This is what the LORD says: “Behold, an army is coming from the land of the north; a great nation is stirred up from the ends of the earth.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD says these words.
A people are coming.
They come from the land of the north.
A great nation rises up.
This nation comes from the farthest parts of the earth.
passages.original: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנֵּ֛ה עַ֥ם בָּ֖א מֵאֶ֣רֶץ צָפ֑וֹן וְג֣וֹי גָּד֔וֹל יֵע֖וֹר מִיַּרְכְּתֵי־ אָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: They grasp the bow and spear; they are cruel and merciless. Their voice roars like the sea, and they ride upon horses, lined up like men in formation against you, O Daughter of Zion.”
passages.sermon:
A great army is coming against you, Daughter of Zion.
This army holds bows and spears.
The soldiers are cruel.
They show no mercy.
Their voices roar like the sea.
They ride on horses.
They stand in formation for battle.
They come to fight against you.
passages.original: קֶ֣שֶׁת וְכִיד֞וֹן יַחֲזִ֗יקוּ אַכְזָרִ֥י הוּא֙ וְלֹ֣א יְרַחֵ֔מוּ קוֹלָם֙ כַּיָּ֣ם יֶהֱמֶ֔ה וְעַל־ סוּסִ֖ים יִרְכָּ֑בוּ עָר֗וּךְ כְּאִישׁ֙ לַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה עָלַ֖יִךְ בַּת־ צִיּֽוֹן׃

passages.text: We have heard the report; our hands hang limp. Anguish has gripped us, pain like that of a woman in labor.
passages.sermon:
We have heard the news.
Our hands have become weak.
Anguish has taken hold of us.
We feel pain like a woman in labor.
passages.original: שָׁמַ֥עְנוּ אֶת־ שָׁמְע֖וֹ רָפ֣וּ יָדֵ֑ינוּ צָרָה֙ הֶחֱזִיקַ֔תְנוּ חִ֖יל כַּיּוֹלֵדָֽה׃

passages.text: Do not go out to the fields; do not walk the road. For the enemy has a sword; terror is on every side.
passages.sermon:
The prophet Jeremiah warns the people of Jerusalem.
He speaks to the people of God.
He says, “Do not go out to the fields.
Do not walk on the road.
The enemy carries a sword.
Terror surrounds you on every side.”
passages.original: אַל־ תֵּצְאִי הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה וּבַדֶּ֖רֶךְ אַל־ תֵּלֵכִי כִּ֚י חֶ֣רֶב לְאֹיֵ֔ב מָג֖וֹר מִסָּבִֽיב׃

passages.text: O daughter of my people, dress yourselves in sackcloth and roll in ashes. Mourn with bitter wailing, as you would for an only son, for suddenly the destroyer will come upon us.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Jerusalem.
He calls them “daughter of my people.”
He commands them to put on sackcloth.
He tells them to roll in ashes.
He tells them to mourn deeply.
He says to mourn as if for an only son.
He commands them to weep with bitter wailing.
He warns them that disaster will come suddenly.
He says the destroyer will come upon them without warning.
passages.original: בַּת־ עַמִּ֤י חִגְרִי־ שָׂק֙ וְהִתְפַּלְּשִׁ֣י בָאֵ֔פֶר אֵ֤בֶל יָחִיד֙ עֲשִׂ֣י לָ֔ךְ מִסְפַּ֖ד תַּמְרוּרִ֑ים כִּ֣י פִתְאֹ֔ם יָבֹ֥א הַשֹּׁדֵ֖ד עָלֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: “I have appointed you to examine My people like ore, so you may know and try their ways.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Jeremiah.
God gives Jeremiah a task.
God appoints Jeremiah to examine the people of Israel.
God tells Jeremiah to test the people as someone tests ore.
God wants Jeremiah to know the ways of the people.
God wants Jeremiah to try and examine their actions.
passages.original: בָּח֛וֹן נְתַתִּ֥יךָ בְעַמִּ֖י מִבְצָ֑ר וְתֵדַ֕ע וּבָחַנְתָּ֖ אֶת־ דַּרְכָּֽם׃

passages.text: All are hardened rebels, walking around as slanderers. They are bronze and iron; all of them are corrupt.
passages.sermon:
The people are hardened rebels.
They refuse to obey.
They walk around as slanderers.
They speak against others.
They are like bronze and iron.
They are strong, but not pure.
All of them are corrupt.
They do evil.
passages.original: כֻּלָּם֙ סָרֵ֣י סֽוֹרְרִ֔ים הֹלְכֵ֥י רָכִ֖יל נְחֹ֣שֶׁת וּבַרְזֶ֑ל כֻּלָּ֥ם מַשְׁחִיתִ֖ים הֵֽמָּה׃

passages.text: The bellows blow fiercely, blasting away the lead with fire. The refining proceeds in vain, for the wicked are not purged.
passages.sermon:
The prophet Jeremiah speaks to the people of Judah.
God compares the people to metal being refined.
The bellows blow with great force.
The fire burns hot and strong.
The lead melts away in the fire.
The refining process continues.
The effort is wasted.
The wicked people do not change.
The evil remains in them.
The refining does not remove their sin.
passages.original: נָחַ֣ר מַפֻּ֔חַ מֵאִשְׁתַּם עֹפָ֑רֶת לַשָּׁוְא֙ צָרַ֣ף צָר֔וֹף וְרָעִ֖ים לֹ֥א נִתָּֽקוּ׃

passages.text: They are called rejected silver, because the LORD has rejected them.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD rejected these people.
People call them rejected silver.
The LORD does not accept them.
They have lost their value to Him.
passages.original: כֶּ֣סֶף נִמְאָ֔ס קָרְא֖וּ לָהֶ֑ם כִּֽי־ מָאַ֥ס יְהוָ֖ה בָּהֶֽם׃פ
